newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks claw back most losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks claw back most losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks halted a seven-session rise Tuesday but recouped most losses at the close on short-covering, dealers said.

"The market got off to a weak start because it had rallied yesterday without Wall Street and today it had to pull back to match the prices of ADRs, reined in by volatility in New York," said Jorge Bonanno of Interfin brokers.
However, a late Wall Street surge helped the blue-chip MerVal index recover from a low of 727 to close at 731.82, shedding 0.3 percent.
Traders said the trend would probably stay erratic ahead of options expirations Friday.

"The market is approaching a near-term ceiling and I think the next few sessions will be volatile," Bonanno said, although he predicted the MerVal might push higher again next week with a target of 745 by the end of February.
Traders said investors were likely to busy themselves squaring options settlements in the next few days.
"We may enter a typical phase of consolidation where the market ignores most local and foreign news and stays more or less rangebound," another trader said.
The broad market index shed 0.3 percent, with losers outpacing winners 35 to 25 and 17 issues closing flat.
Floor volume recovered to 31.2 million pesos from Monday's slim tally of 20.3 million, while over-the-counter deals shrank to 61.8 million from 116.4 million Monday.

Top main-tier performers were construction stock Polledo, which surged 4.9 percent, and gas firm Transportadora de Gas del Sur, up 1.5 percent. Losers were led by power utility Central Costanera, foods giant Molinos and Banco de Galicia, off 2.5 percent, 1.8 percent and 1.5 percent respectively.
